hints.title: Wildcard Branching Explosion Obstacle
hints.text: Branching recursively on every wildcard produces exponential 3^N states. Can you track the lowest and highest possible count of open brackets simultaneously in linear time?

hints.title: Open Count Interval Invariant
hints.text: The count of open brackets forms a continuous integer interval [cmin, cmax]. If cmax drops below 0, invalid closing occurred. At the end, the string is valid if cmin reaches 0.

hints.title: Range Evolution Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through the string. On '(', increment both cmin and cmax. On ')', decrement both. On '*', decrement cmin (treating as ')') and increment cmax (treating as '('). If cmax becomes negative, return false. Clamp cmin to at least 0. Finally return true if cmin equals 0.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Single linear pass tracking the feasible interval of unclosed open parentheses.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exhaustive branching on each wildcard '*' yields 3^N combinations, timing out for N >= 30.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking upper and lower bounds replaces exponential recursion with strict O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that reachable open parentheses counts form a contiguous range without gaps.
